title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Retention, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows & Risk Exceptions
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
=======
This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s security and compliance prescriptions for: role-based access control (RBAC) and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure software development lifecycle (SDLC) controls, incident response (security-focused), compliance evidence workflows, and the risk & exceptions process. It is intended for engineering, security, product, and compliance stakeholders who own or operate production inference services and customer-facing controls.

Scope
-----
Applies to: Redwood-hosted services, Dedicated control planes, Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments where Redwood is responsible for the control plane or provides managed operational guidance.
Not in scope: customer-managed application logic and customer data within fully air-gapped on-prem installs where Redwood has no access.

Principles
----------
- Least privilege: grant the minimum permissions required for a role or task.
- Auditability: actions that affect confidentiality, integrity, or availability must be logged with tamper-evident controls.
- Regional compliance: honor region-specific residency and retention requirements; surface options to customers.
- Defense in depth: combine RBAC, MFA, secrets management, and cryptographic protections.

1) RBAC and Authentication
---------------------------
Overview
- Primary identity provider: Okta (SCIM + SSO) for staff.
- Service identities: short-lived tokens for infra automation, PKI-backed service certificates for internal mTLS where applicable.
- Privileged access requires MFA (hardware or TOTP + phishing-resistant when available).

Roles and ownership
- Roles: Viewer, Developer, Operator, Security, Billing Admin, Support, Platform Admin.
- Owners: each role has a documented team owner in the Team Roster. Security owns Platform Admin role approvals and periodic reviews.

Provisioning and lifecycle (procedure)
1. Access request via Jira service-desk with justification and ticket tags (access:rbac).
2. Manager approval + security approval for any role >= Operator.
3. SCIM provisioning is performed automatically; manual provisioning allowed for contractors with expiration.
4. Default expiry: 90 days for elevated roles; renewals require re-approval.
5. Quarterly access review (owners must attest).

Service accounts and automation
- Use short-lived service tokens issued by internal STS. Long-lived keys are prohibited unless approved as exception.
- All service accounts must be tagged with owner, purpose, and rotation schedule.

Key controls and metrics
- Access review cadence: quarterly.
- Compliance target: 100% of Operator/Platform Admin accounts reviewed each quarter.
- Deprovisioning SLA: 24 hours after termination ticket is filed.

2) Audit Logging
----------------
What we log
- Authentication events (SSO login, token issuance/revocation, MFA failures).
- Authorization decisions (RBAC checks, policy evaluations, role assignments).
- Administrative configuration changes (model catalog changes, routing policy changes, rollout changes).
- Data-access events: access to customer request/response payloads, secrets access, KMS operations.
- System-level telemetry needed for incident investigation (scheduler actions, autoscaling, kernel failures).

Logging pipeline and storage
- Central pipeline: logs -> Fluentd -> secure S3 (WORM-enabled buckets for audit logs) -> indexer (Datadog/Splunk/ELK depending on environment).
- Integrity: CRC checks, object immutability for audit logs, and periodic hash verification.

Retention matrix (default, configurable per-customer/legal need)
- Auth + authorization events: 7 years (default for audit compliance).
- Audit configuration changes: 7 years.
- System telemetry/metrics (aggregated): 1 year.
- Request bodies (customer workloads): default 30 days; retention can be altered per contract (customers may request 0 retention).
- Debug traces & profile dumps: 90 days unless escalated to evidence.

SLOs and alerts
- Log ingestion SLO: 99.9% of platform audit log events indexed within 2 minutes.
- Alerting: failed log-forwarder, checksum drift, or bucket write errors trigger P1 to eng-sre and security.

3) Data Residency & Retention
----------------------------
Residency model
- By default, customer request data and derived artifacts (embeddings, caching keys) are stored in the customer-selected region (US, EU, APAC regions supported).
- Control plane metadata may be stored in a globally replicated control plane; customer-sensitive fields are redacted unless contractually required.

Retention policy (summary)
- Customer request payloads: default 30 days; per-customer contracts may specify 0 days or longer.
- Embeddings and cached prefixes: retention configurable; default 90 days.
- Audit logs and configuration snapshots: 7 years.
- Backups: encrypted, retention per backup policy (typically 90 days for ephemeral infra state; 7 years for compliance snapshots).

Cross-border transfer controls
- Any transfer of EU customer data outside EU requires documented lawful basis (e.g., SCCs) and is only performed when requested/contracted.
- Private deployments: avoid cross-border transfers unless customer explicitly permits.

4) Secure SDLC (Development and Release Controls)
-------------------------------------------------
Minimum controls
- Code review required for all changes; two approvers for changes touching production infra or auth/RBAC logic.
- Static analysis (SAST) and dependency scanning in CI for every PR.
- Secret scanning on all branches; detection blocks merge on prod-facing repos.
- Build and signing: release artifacts signed and stored in an artifact registry.
- Infrastructure-as-code changes require plan review and guarded apply with multi-person approval for prod.

Release checklist (required for all production deploys)
- Automated test coverage threshold met.
- Security scans passing or documented risk acceptance.
- Rollout plan: canary + metrics, rollback playbook attached.
- Observability: dashboards and alerts for any changed service.

Dependency & vulnerability handling
- Vulnerabilities with severity >=7.5 (CVSS) must be remediated within 14 days or have an approved mitigation/exception.

5) Incident Response — Security Procedures
-----------------------------------------
Objectives
- Detect, contain, eradicate, and recover with evidence preservation.

Roles & contacts
- Incident Commander (IC): assigned from eng-sre.
- Security lead: Security on-call.
- Communications: Legal + Comms for external notifications.
- Customer success: for affected customer notifications.

Initial response timeline
1. Detection/alert routing (automatic): 0-15 minutes.
2. Initial triage and incident declaration: within 1 hour.
3. Escalation to IC + security lead: within 1 hour.
4. Customer notification (if customer-affecting): initial notification within 4 hours for critical incidents per contract; follow-up timeline per SLA.

Forensic and evidence preservation steps
- Isolate affected instances; create immutable snapshots of affected disks and logs.
- Preserve relevant audit logs and configuration snapshots in the evidence repository (WORM S3).
- Collect process and network dumps; never overwrite original artifacts.

Post-incident
- Produce a postmortem within 7 business days with impact, root cause, timeline, mitigations, and action items owner-tagged. Security and SRE must review and approve the remediation plan.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
--------------------------------
Evidence cataloging
- Controls must map to evidence artifacts (config exports, screenshots, signed attestations, scans). Each control entry requires an evidence_owner.

Quarterly readiness & audit process
1. Evidence owners run the Evidence Readiness checklist 30 days before quarter-end.
2. Required artifacts are uploaded to the secure evidence bucket and linked in the controlbook.
3. Internal compliance team performs spot-checks; elevated gaps flagged for risk board.

Evidence lifecycle
- Evidence artifacts retained per control requirements (default 7 years for audit logs/config exports).
- Access to the evidence bucket: RBAC-protected and reviewed monthly.

7) Risk & Exceptions Process
----------------------------
When to file an exception
- When a required control cannot be implemented within the timeline (technical limitation, customer need, legacy dependency).

Exception workflow (procedure)
1. Submit an Exception Request ticket with: scope, risk statement, compensating controls, mitigation timeline, and owner.
2. Security reviews and returns an initial determination within 5 business days.
3. For high-risk exceptions, the Risk Review Board (Security, Legal, Product, Eng SRE) makes a decision; approvals are time-limited (max 90 days) and documented.
4. Exception renewals require re-evaluation and evidence of mitigation progress.

Compensating controls examples
- Enhanced monitoring and alerting, additional encryption, IP allowlists, dedicated tenancy, or shorter retention windows.

Metrics and reporting
- Exception inventory updated weekly; report daily for critical exceptions to exec staff.
